description: The providers the factory may consider, and what each is permitted to receive. `packages/control-plane/src/provider-routing.js` is the code that reads this; `config/model-execution.json` is still the switch that decides whether any provider call may happen at all. This file narrows a field, it does not open a lane: every profile here is refused while the kill switch is off, and a profile with `ready: false` is refused regardless.
rules: Deny-by-default, twice over. A profile grants nothing until it names the data classes it may receive AND the roles it has earned. An empty `eligibleRoles` is the committed state for every provider whose canary has not run, and it means the provider cannot be selected for anything.

`allowedDataClasses` is a ceiling set by policy review, not by capability. A provider does not become eligible for private material because it is technically capable of receiving it, and widening this list is a reviewed change to this file with `policyReviewedAt` and `policySource` filled in.

A high-risk role is a separate grant. `eligibleRoles` may approve a provider for cheap bounded work; security, release promotion, destructive-change review, architecture sign-off and visual promotion additionally require the role in `highRiskRolesApproved`. One list would make that guard cosmetic, because whatever edit granted the cheap role would have granted the dangerous one too.

Unclassified tasks route nowhere. `resolveDataClass` treats absent or unrecognised classification as `private-business`, so material nobody classified cannot reach a provider approved only for public material.
Free is a refusal, not a discount. `costMode: free-only` means a request that would become billable is refused rather than paid for. Exhausting a free allowance does not authorise spending money.

Quotas are observed, never declared. Nothing here records how many requests a free tier allows, because those numbers change without notice; the provider's own response at runtime is the authority, and a 429 is a refusal with a name rather than a surprise.
A credential is a reference. `secretRef` names where the trusted gateway looks. No value belongs in this file, in any environment file committed beside it, or in an attempt record.

profiles.note: The existing canary provider, described here so selection sees one field rather than two. It is `metered` because the key is billable, and its data classes are the same conservative set as everything else: no provider terms have been reviewed and recorded yet, and the first canary uses a synthetic fixture, so nothing needs a wider class today.

The preferred first free-provider canary: it publishes explicit free-plan limits and returns a standard 429 with rate-limit metadata, which makes it a real exercise of the fallback path rather than a happy-path demo. Those limits are deliberately not copied here. No private data class is approved merely because an API exists.

profiles.policySource: Google's Gemini API pricing documentation distinguishes Free Tier from Paid Tier and states Free Tier data may be used to improve Google's products.
profiles.note: Restricted to public, synthetic and sanitised material for the reason recorded in policySource, and that restriction is not to be widened without an explicit operator policy decision recorded here.

profiles.policySource: OpenRouter transmits inputs to selected or automatically selected underlying providers, whose retention and training practices differ from each other.
profiles.note: Emergency breadth, deliberately last and deliberately unconfigured. `modelId` is null on purpose: a pinned model must be chosen before this profile can be selected at all, because the data policy that matters is the underlying provider's and `openrouter/free` does not name one. Not the first continuity mechanism.

An explicit extension point, not a supported provider. No adapter, no endpoint and no approved data class, so it is refused as not-configured. It is recorded here rather than omitted so that adding it later is filling in a profile rather than rediscovering the shape of one. The continuity programme does not wait for it.
